title: Developer repository loader and credential theft patterns

sources.scope: Hijacked npm releases, exact versions, loader behavior
Unauthorized Git pushes, hidden VS Code tasks, staged font loaders, persistence

behavioral_checks.label: Suspicious startup script
behavioral_checks.basis: npm lifecycle or dev/build commands execute an unusual local loader

behavioral_checks.label: Hidden editor task
behavioral_checks.basis: VS Code folderOpen task can execute node or concealed payloads

behavioral_checks.label: Disguised executable asset
behavioral_checks.basis: font-like file contains source code rather than a recognized font header

behavioral_checks.label: Dynamic code execution
behavioral_checks.basis: configuration decodes or retrieves script content and evaluates it

behavioral_checks.label: Sensitive-file ignore change
behavioral_checks.basis: gitignore explicitly reincludes a private environment file

behavioral_checks.label: Suspicious config loader
behavioral_checks.basis: build or lint configuration has combined code-loader traits

behavioral_checks.label: Known loader artifacts
behavioral_checks.basis: specific npm-ws loader artifact filenames exist in home directory

behavioral_checks.label: Known malicious npm release
behavioral_checks.basis: exact resolved package and release appears in a known published advisory

behavioral_checks.label: Unusual propagation script
behavioral_checks.basis: unexpected auto-push batch file exists; content not executed

known_limits: Only exact npm package versions are matched; no semver range inference.
A matching lockfile entry cannot prove execution or credential theft.
Pattern matches are leads, not confirmation of compromise.
Changed remote branches and running process persistence require separate evidence.
Do not execute scripts or contact command-and-control infrastructure.
